blocks.title: Divide and conquer
blocks.text: Divide and conquer breaks a large problem into smaller, similar parts, solves each part independently, and combines their solutions to solve the original problem.
Merge Sort is a classic example: divide the unsorted list into two halves, sort each half, then merge the two sorted halves into the final sorted list. Merge Sort runs in O(n log n) time.

blocks.alt: Merge sort tree of blue boxes: [14, 7, 3, 12] is divided into [14, 7] and [3, 12]; each of these is divided into single items 14, 7 and 3, 12; the bottom row shows the sorted list 3, 7, 12, 14.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.6: Merge Sort Process (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.6; the single items under [14, 7] shown as 14, 7).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 3.6 shows [14, 7] divided into 7 and 14; dividing does not change the order, so the single items are 14 and 7, as drawn above.
